title: Milan’s bishop bargains with a usurper
spotify: The History of Rome 155 The New Bishop of Milan
description: Mike Duncan’s The History of Rome reaches 383, when Milan was an imperial capital and its new bishop, Ambrose, helped negotiate a power-sharing deal with the rebel general Magnus Maximus. Ambrose lies in the crypt of the Basilica of Sant’Ambrogio.

title: A family of lords tightens its grip on the city
episode: 113 – The definitive death of communal Milan (1339 – 1354)
spotify: A History of Italy 113 The definitive death of communal Milan 1339 1354
description: When Azzone Visconti died in 1339, his uncles Luchino and Giovanni took over Milan and kept expanding it, ending the old self-governing commune. Azzone’s marble tomb is in San Gottardo in Corte, the church of his palace behind the Royal Palace.

title: A mercenary becomes duke and builds a hospital for the poor
episode: 152 - Duke Francesco Sforza and his sex-crazed son (1450 - 1568)
place: Ca’ Granda, the former Ospedale Maggiore
spotify: A History of Italy 152 Duke Francesco Sforza and his sexcrazed son 1450 1568
description: Mark Rasmussen follows Francesco Sforza, the mercenary captain who became Duke of Milan in 1450, and his dissolute son Galeazzo Maria. Francesco founded the Ospedale Maggiore, the vast hospital now called Ca’ Granda and used by the University of Milan.

title: Leonardo paints a castle hall into a forest
episode: Ep. 66: Leonardo da Vinci in the Sforza Court
spotify: The Italian Renaissance Podcast Ep 66 Leonardo da Vinci in the Sforza Court
description: Leonardo da Vinci spent most of his early career serving Ludovico Sforza, “il Moro,” regent and then Duke of Milan. In the Castello Sforzesco, the ducal castle, he painted the Sala delle Asse as an arbour of interlaced mulberry branches.

title: An opera house named after the church it replaced
show: Stuff You Missed in History Class
episode: SYMHC Classics:  La Scala Opera House
spotify: Stuff You Missed in History Class SYMHC Classics La Scala Opera House
description: Holly Frey and Tracy V. Wilson’s 2014 episode on the Teatro alla Scala, opened in 1778 on the site of the demolished church of Santa Maria alla Scala. Verdi’s Otello and Puccini’s Madama Butterfly both premiered at the opera house.

title: Forty minutes in front of the Last Supper
episode: Leonardo da Vinci, The Last Supper
place: Last Supper refectory, Santa Maria delle Grazie
spotify: Painting of the Week Podcast Leonardo da Vinci The Last Supper
description: Hosts Phil and Laura take apart Leonardo da Vinci’s Last Supper, painted in the 1490s on the dining-hall wall of the Santa Maria delle Grazie convent in an experimental oil-and-tempera technique that began flaking within decades.

title: Saffron, a prank and a yellow wedding rice
description: Sauced traces risotto alla milanese, Milan’s saffron rice, from saffron fraud in medieval Nuremberg to the story of a glassmaker’s apprentice on the Duomo cathedral’s windows who, legend says, tinted a 1574 wedding risotto yellow as a joke.

title: An anarchist falls from a police station window
episode: #582 | Piazza Fontana & The Accidental Death of An Anarchist
spotify: English Learning for Curious Minds 582 Piazza Fontana The Accidental Death of An Anarchist
description: Held after the 1969 Piazza Fontana bank bombing, anarchist Giuseppe Pinelli fell to his death from the police headquarters on Via Fatebenefratelli. An English-learning show on the case and Dario Fo’s satirical play Accidental Death of an Anarchist.

title: A fashion heir is shot on his office steps
spotify: Witness History The murder of Maurizio Gucci
apple: Witness History The murder of Maurizio Gucci
description: On 27 March 1995 Maurizio Gucci, former head of the fashion house, was shot dead outside his office on Via Palestro. Rachel Naylor talks to Carmine Gallo, the detective who tied the killing to his ex-wife Patrizia Reggiani and her clairvoyant.

title: The Argentine coach who taught Inter to defend
episode: Herrera's Inter Milan: The Birth of the Catenaccio
spotify: It Was What It Was Herreras Inter Milan The Birth of the Catenaccio
description: Football writers Jonathan Wilson and Rob Draper on Helenio Herrera, the Argentine coach whose Inter won the European Cup in 1964 and 1965 with catenaccio, a defence-first system. Inter play at San Siro stadium, which they share with AC Milan.

title: Sculpted family tombs in the city of the dead
show: History Goes Bump: Ghost Tours For The Mind
episode: Stones and Bones Ep. 18 - Monumental Cemetery in Milan
spotify: History Goes Bump Ghost Tours For The Mind Stones and Bones Ep 18 Monumental Cemetery in Milan
description: History Goes Bump, a podcast on haunted history, tours the Cimitero Monumentale, opened in 1866 and filled with sculpted tombs of Milan’s industrial families. Novelist Alessandro Manzoni is buried in its Famedio, a hall of fame by the main gate.

title: Art nouveau, Milan style, around Porta Venezia
spotify: Listen To MI Architecture in Milan 1 The Liberty style
description: Listen To MI, a podcast from Milan’s house museums, looks at Liberty, the Italian art nouveau of about 1900, in the Porta Venezia district. The style’s best-known building there is Giuseppe Sommaruga’s Palazzo Castiglioni on Corso Venezia.

title: An architect’s flats for a couple of collectors
episode: Architecture in Milan - 2 - Piero Portaluppi: The Boschi Di Stefano House Museum and Villa Necchi Campiglio
place: Casa Museo Boschi Di Stefano, Via Jan
spotify: Listen To MI Architecture in Milan 2 Piero Portaluppi The Boschi Di Stefano House Museum and Villa Necchi Campiglio
description: Architect Piero Portaluppi shaped interwar Milan. This episode visits his buildings that are open to the public, among them the Casa Museo Boschi Di Stefano, a couple’s flat hung floor to ceiling with 20th-century Italian art.

title: A fake apse less than a metre deep
episode: Architecture in Milan - 4 - Bramante and Filarete, Renaissance geniuses
place: Santa Maria presso San Satiro church
spotify: Listen To MI Architecture in Milan 4 Bramante and Filarete Renaissance geniuses
description: Two Renaissance architects in Milan: Filarete, designer of the Ospedale Maggiore hospital, and Donato Bramante. At Santa Maria presso San Satiro church, Bramante painted and modelled a deep choir behind the altar into a wall less than a metre deep.

title: A fashion editor invents the concept store
episode: Fashion in Milan - 4 - Corso Como 10 and the birth of the Concept Store
spotify: Listen To MI Fashion in Milan 4 Corso Como 10 and the birth of the Concept Store
description: Carla Sozzani, former fashion magazine editor, tells how she opened 10 Corso Como in 1990, a gallery, bookshop, boutique and café around a courtyard that is often called the first concept store.

title: A poet’s canal and the writers around it
episode: Literature in Milan - 4 - The Navigli Area
place: Alda Merini’s home, Naviglio Grande canal
spotify: Listen To MI Literature in Milan 4 The Navigli Area
description: A literary walk along the Navigli, Milan’s old canals, starting with poet Alda Merini, who lived for decades on the Ripa di Porta Ticinese beside the Naviglio Grande and wrote about the asylum where she spent years.

title: Why the furniture world descends on Milan each April
episode: Why Milan design week is such a big deal
spotify: Dezeen Weekly Why Milan design week is such a big deal
description: Editors at the architecture and design magazine Dezeen explain why Milan design week matters: the Salone del Mobile furniture fair at the Fiera Milano grounds in Rho, plus hundreds of satellite shows around the city known as the Fuorisalone.
